summary: Session 2 of 4: the TreeDataProvider, shipped as a COMPLETE VERTICAL SLICE behind the existing surface. A native TreeView renders four levels lazily (module -> status bucket -> session set -> SESSION, the operator's 2026-08-04 ask 1), with a real hierarchical context menu built from contributes.submenus, contextValue-gated actions covering the whole ROW_ACTIONS registry, per-theme status glyphs, and the webview's left-click behaviour preserved. The webview tree remains FIRST and DEFAULT per the spec; the native view is contributed collapsed beneath it so Session 3 switches over rather than builds. The fourth level costs NO additional disk read: the scan already parsed and then discarded the sessions[] ledger, and normalizeLedgerSessions now retains it. THE FINDING OF THIS SESSION IS THAT BOTH PRIOR RECOMMENDATIONS ON THE STATUS ICONS WERE WRONG. S1 and the routed step-3.5 analyst independently recommended re-authoring the four SVGs to fill:currentColor, the analyst at HIGH confidence while also saying it must be verified by running. Both reasoned from the activity-bar mark, which VS Code renders through a different mechanism. icon-render-mechanism.spec.ts measured a real Extension Development Host: TreeItem.iconPath renders as background-image with mask-image:none, so currentColor resolves against the SVG's own document and would have painted every glyph one fixed colour on both themes - worse than the defect it was meant to cure, and it would have shipped looking deliberate. The {light, dark} pair the operator authored into media/light and media/dark is what ships, and statusIconAssets.test.ts keeps currentColor out as an executable gate rather than advice. Two defects were caught in self-review that no other gate would have seen: missing stable TreeItem.ids (the 30-second poll would have collapsed the tree roughly twice a minute, since VS Code keys expansion state on id and derives one from the label, and bucket labels repeat under every module), and empty bucket rows offering a twisty that opens onto nothing. S1's assigned residual is discharged: utils/startupTiming.ts emits module-load / activate() / resolveWebviewView() / first-tree-roots to DABBLER_STARTUP_TIMING_PATH, so S4 can produce a per-bucket before/after. First paint is deliberately NOT instrumented - the host cannot see when a row becomes visible, Layer 3 observes it from the DOM for both implementations through one protocol, and the emitted payload says so in a note field that a test asserts. One duplication was REMOVED rather than added: the module assembly and bucket ordering are now shared by both Explorer surfaces (moduleAssembly.assembleVisibleModules, SessionSetsModel.orderedBuckets), so the two views shipped side by side cannot disagree about grouping or order. The dead iconUriFor helper went with the legacy media/*.svg copies. VERIFICATION: discovery round 1 (fan-out 2, both gpt-5-6-sol, anthropic auto-excluded) returned VERIFIED with ZERO blocking findings and 12 nits, five raised convergently by both calls. All 12 were fixed despite the round being non-blocking - two were real correctness defects (duplicate/non-positive session numbers colliding row identity via TreeItem.id; webview resolve marks not first-wins, so a hide/re-expand would silently replace the startup figure S4 quotes). A 13TH finding came from running the suite rather than from the round: real-host-baseline.spec.ts was OVERWRITING s1-real-host-baseline.json, S1's committed measurement of record and the basis of the operator's S4 startup gate. S1's artifact was restored unmodified, the re-run kept as separate S2 evidence (a third independent reproduction, agreeing within ~2% and reproducing S1's flatness finding), and the write gated behind DABBLER_WRITE_EVIDENCE=1 - the same class as the icon-probe nit, fixed at every sibling site. Discovery round 2 then re-reviewed the SHIPPED state, because round 1's verdict covered code that was subsequently changed; remediation-review correctly refused, since a zero-finding round records no baseline to review a fix against. TESTS: Layer 2 1907 passing / 0 failing (8 new suites); Layer 3 FULL suite 32 passed / 0 failed including both new native-tree specs, re-run green against the post-remediation build. Typecheck clean. Lint 7 errors / 61 warnings, ALL pre-existing in files this session does not touch. NO PERFORMANCE CLAIM IS MADE. The native tree exists but was not measured against the webview; S1 withdrew the performance pitch in writing and S4 owns the number and the operator's sub-second gate. Nothing is released this session.

reason.specifics: Both routed analysts converge on Claude for Session 3, and the S1 analyst's reasoning is the better-argued route: S3 is a deletion plus a re-expression of a behavioural specification, not greenfield authoring. The S2 analyst reached the same engine on reasoning this session REJECTS on the record - that S3 is 'primarily file deletion and minor package.json edits, which are highly mechanical.' All three S1 panelists independently named S3 the riskiest session in the set, and the operator imposed an internal ordering (write the new suites, prove them green, seed a regression and prove the new Layer 3 catches it, and ONLY THEN delete) precisely because it is not mechanical. Budget: DABBLER_* provider keys for routed calls; zero engine-seat capacity, which the operator has been cutting back. Session 2 leaves S3 a working slice to switch to rather than a data adapter to finish, so the switchover is a package.json reordering plus deletions - see s2-implementation-notes.md section 7 for exactly what must die and what must survive.
